title: The Agent Awakens: Collaborative Development with Copilot - Christopher Harrison, GitHub
talk_summary: A GitHub DevRel hands-on lab on Copilot coding agent, covering how to give it context (instructions files, MCP servers), how its sandboxed GitHub Actions environment is locked down, and how to iterate when it gets things wrong.

takeaways.technique: Repo-level copilot-instructions.md as durable agent context
takeaways.what_they_do: A checked-in instructions file gives the agent app overview, code standards, pre-commit requirements, language guidance, and repo structure; it is read on every chat request and by the coding agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I have copilot-instructions.md. This is looked at by coding agent, and it's also looked at by every single chat request that I make inside the IDE.

takeaways.technique: Scoped instruction files with apply-to globs and chaining
takeaways.what_they_do: Small .instructions files are auto-applied by path pattern (e.g. test_*.py, *.tsx) and can reference other instruction files, avoiding one giant file.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can create a dot instructions file... even point to prototype files... if it's inside the server test folder and starts with test underscore, it's going to automatically apply that.

takeaways.technique: Ephemeral per-task sandbox with no internet and branch-only write
takeaways.what_they_do: Each assigned issue gets its own fresh GitHub Actions environment, no external network by default, write access only to its own branch, and PR left in draft until a human approves workflow runs.

takeaways.technique: Author cannot review own work; draft PR gated on explicit approval
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent that produced the change is barred from reviewing it; a different party must approve, and CI/security checks don't run until someone clicks approve.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you assign an issue to coding agent, you are not allowed to then review its work. So you need somebody else to review its work.

takeaways.technique: Iterate via comment, or unassign/reassign to reset cleanly
takeaways.what_they_do: When output is wrong, either comment to continue the same session, or unassign and reassign the agent to start a completely fresh session from scratch.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just unassign Copilot, change your issue, and then reassign Copilot... that way it will just completely start from from scratch.

takeaways.technique: MCP servers for external data, vetted and pinned in repo config
takeaways.what_they_do: MCP servers expose commands so the agent can query external systems; config lives in a repo mcp.json, credentials are per-user, and the speaker stresses vetting servers before granting action rights.
